name: flask-eval-v1
description: Questions about the Flask library source (src/flask) with manually verified expected files and symbols, pinned to one commit.

methodology.scope: Only files under src/flask/ are ever ground truth; tests, docs and examples never are.
methodology.primary: The file(s) where the behaviour the question asks about is implemented: the one-line answer. For definition questions, every file that defines the named symbol. For caller and dependency questions, the files on the other end of the call sites / import edges (the answer itself).
methodology.supporting: Other files a complete answer must also cite to be correct: triggers, hand-offs and base implementations, included only when the question's wording asks for that step. Omit test: if a correct, complete answer could leave a file out, the file is not listed at all. A file that merely calls the primary code is never listed outside caller questions.
methodology.relevant_symbols: Qualified names of the functions/classes/methods that implement the answer (for chunk-level scoring); each must live in a primary or supporting file. Empty when the answer is module-level code.
methodology.category: definition: where is a named symbol defined. caller: what calls/uses a named symbol. dependency: which modules import / are imported by a named module. concept: where is a described behaviour implemented. flow: how does a described multi-step process work.
methodology.difficulty: Structural, from the shape of the ground truth, assigned by a fixed rubric (checked by the validator): named questions (definition/caller/dependency) are easy with 1 file, medium with 2-3, hard with 4+; described questions (concept/flow) are medium with 1 file and hard with 2+. It measures how much must be found and combined, not how a retrieval system performs; the benchmark reports whether the two agree.
methodology.callers: Call sites (including passing a method as a callback) found by searching src/flask; definitions and docstring mentions excluded.
methodology.dependency: Edges of the import graph of src/flask, extracted with the Tree-sitter parser with relative imports resolved. Imports inside TYPE_CHECKING blocks count.
methodology.freeze: Once frozen, the questions are never edited to suit retrieval results. The validator checks a fingerprint of the questions. A factual correction must be published as a new dataset version with a changelog.
methodology.verification: Each entry's evidence field cites the lines read at the pinned commit. python -m app.evaluation.validate re-checks that files and symbols exist.

questions.question: What code runs when a Flask application object is constructed?
questions.evidence: Both primary, neither is a thin delegate: Flask.__init__ (app.py:311) sets up the CLI group and static route after super().__init__; App.__init__ (sansio/app.py:279-408) does the bulk of initialisation.

questions.question: Where are environment variables with a FLASK_ prefix loaded into the app config?

questions.question: How does Flask look up which registered error handler should handle an exception?
questions.evidence: The whole lookup (blueprint vs app, code vs class, MRO walk) is App._find_error_handler (sansio/app.py:868-891). Its callers in app.py are not needed to answer it, so they are not listed.

questions.question: Where is URL routing performed for an incoming request?
questions.evidence: AppContext.match_request (ctx.py:405-414) calls url_adapter.match and stores the rule/args or routing exception; run from AppContext.push (:444). create_url_adapter (app.py:510) only builds the adapter and is not needed to answer, so it is not listed.

questions.question: Where does a blueprint copy its routes and handlers into the application?

questions.question: Where are flashed messages stored?

questions.question: Where are `request` and `g` added to the template context before a template is rendered?
questions.evidence: Primary: _default_template_ctx_processor (templating.py:21-33) returns {'g': ctx.g} and, in a request, 'request': ctx.request (session is NOT added here; it is a Jinja global set in create_jinja_environment, app.py:504). Supporting: Flask.update_template_context (app.py:591-619) is what runs the processors before rendering (called from templating.py:125, :167).

questions.question: Where are teardown functions called when a context is popped?

questions.question: How is an incoming WSGI request dispatched to a view function?
questions.evidence: Primary: wsgi_app (app.py:1569) -> full_dispatch_request (:1600) -> dispatch_request (:1019) -> view_functions[endpoint] (:993). Supporting: AppContext.push (ctx.py:416) runs match_request (:444), which sets the url_rule dispatch_request uses; without it the answer cannot say how the view is chosen.

questions.question: How is the user's session loaded at the start of a request and saved at the end?
questions.evidence: Primary: loading and saving are implemented by open_session (sessions.py:323) and save_session (:337). Supporting: the question asks when, which is AppContext.push -> _get_session -> open_session (ctx.py:439, :388) at the start and Flask.process_response -> save_session (app.py:1419) at the end.

questions.question: How does the `@app.route` decorator register a URL rule?
questions.evidence: Primary: the rule is created and added to url_map by App.add_url_rule (sansio/app.py:604-661, url_map.add at :653). Supporting: the decorator Scaffold.route (sansio/scaffold.py:343) is the entry point the question names and calls add_url_rule (:370).

questions.question: How does a blueprint get registered on an app and its routes added?
questions.evidence: Primary: Blueprint.register (sansio/blueprints.py:273-377) builds a BlueprintSetupState and runs the deferred functions (:334) that call app.add_url_rule (:110). Supporting: App.register_blueprint (sansio/app.py:569) is the entry point that delegates to it (:595).

questions.question: How does Flask convert a view's return value into a response object?
questions.evidence: finalize_request (app.py:1024) calls make_response (:1042); Flask.make_response is app.py:1227-1367.

questions.question: How are before_request and after_request callbacks executed?
questions.evidence: Executed by preprocess_request (app.py:1388-1390) and process_response (:1414-1416, reversed). The decorators that register them (Scaffold.before_request/after_request) are not needed to explain execution, so they are not listed.

questions.question: What happens when a view raises an unhandled exception?
questions.evidence: Primary: full_dispatch_request catches it (app.py:1020) -> handle_user_exception (:868); if re-raised, wsgi_app calls handle_exception (:1603, def :900). Supporting: handler selection is App._find_error_handler (sansio/app.py:868), which decides whether a registered handler runs.

questions.question: How does the `flask run` command start the development server?
questions.evidence: run_command (cli.py:882) calls info.load_app() (:955), reads get_debug_flag (:973) and calls run_simple (:983).

questions.question: How does the Flask command line find the application to load?
questions.evidence: ScriptInfo.load_app (cli.py:333) calls prepare_import (:348) and locate_app (:349); locate_app calls find_best_app (:262).

questions.question: How does the test client send a request to the application?
questions.evidence: FlaskClient.open (testing.py:204) builds a request via EnvironBuilder (:197, :217) and calls super().open (:235).

questions.question: How does `url_for` build a URL for an endpoint?
questions.evidence: Primary: the URL is built by Flask.url_for (app.py:1105-1225, using create_url_adapter at :1185). Supporting: helpers.url_for (helpers.py:200), the public function the question names, delegates to current_app.url_for (:244).
